mentions.heading: Increased tariffs and government restrictions could reduce demand for our products
mentions.detail: China restrictions on raw materials and Micron-containing products; possible revived antidumping probe on US analog chips; buy-Chinese directives
mentions.quote: The Chinese government may also re-initiate the suspended antidumping investigation into imports of analog chips originating in the United States and aggressively enforce the new regulation intended to combat the extraterritorial application of foreign trade controls, sanctions and other measures

mentions.heading: Evolving U.S. export controls may harm competitiveness
mentions.detail: Non-US customers may shift to suppliers not subject to US export controls; foreign competitors gain investment
mentions.quote: It is also possible that evolving U.S. export controls may encourage our non-U.S. customers to purchase from companies not subject to U.S. export controls, thereby harming our business, market position, and financial results.

mentions.heading: Trade barriers may limit access to equipment and raw materials
mentions.detail: Retaliatory trade measures could limit access to rare earth minerals, equipment, components and M&A approvals
mentions.quote: Further changes in trade or national security protection policy, tariffs, additional taxes, restrictions on exports or other trade barriers, including those taken against the U.S. in retaliation for U.S. policies, may limit our ability to obtain equipment, components or raw materials (including rare earth minerals), limit our ability to produce products

mentions.heading: Outcome of income tax examinations and disputes
mentions.detail: IRS transfer pricing disputes fiscal 2007-2015 settled September 2025; returns open from fiscal 2007
mentions.quote: The disputed amounts for fiscal 2013 to fiscal 2016 largely relate to transfer pricing matters. In December 2023, we filed a petition in the U.S. Tax Court challenging the 2014 to 2015 Notice. In September 2025, we reached a settlement with the IRS for fiscal 2007 to fiscal 2015.

mentions.heading: Malaysian tax assessment dispute
mentions.detail: Malaysian IRB fiscal 2020 assessment up to MYR 1.9 billion (~$480.2 million); decision possibly within 18 months
mentions.quote: If the adjustment is upheld by the highest court that has jurisdiction over this matter in Malaysia, it could result in income taxes and penalties up to MYR 1.9 billion (approximately $480.2 million based on the exchange rate as of March 31, 2026).

mentions.heading: Exposure to greater income tax liabilities and tax law changes
mentions.quote: We are a U.S.-based multinational company subject to tax in many U.S. and foreign jurisdictions. Our income tax obligations could be affected by many factors, including changes to our operating structure, intercompany arrangements and tax planning strategies.
